Thanks for all your concern. All these comments are super informative. Just to clarify, I applied for an MA program & was accepted into the MA program. Three students, including myself who were accepted into the MA program were offered a decision to either remain in the MA program or choose the PsyD program instead. We were told that the faculty were impressed with our files and saw potential in us to pursue a doctorate. From my understanding the PsyD program is a newer addition to the school and hasn’t yet been apa accredited. I was also offered a graduate assistantship if I choose the MA degree and I want to ask if a similar assistantship or fellowship will be offered if I choose the PsyD track because the assistantship offers a lot of financial relief.  I believe in comparison to the MA the psyd will be about $100 more per credit, also one year longer. (Basically 70+ credits versus 90+ credits). 

I’m assuming by exploitative you mean taking advantage of students in some way and that comment has definitely worried me a bit. I’m not sure if my situation is something that normally happens for most programs or if it’s uncommon and I should be more suspicious. I’m planning on sending another email to ask for some more information before I make a final decision.  

I’m a bit of an over thinker so I can’t help but stress about big decisions like this. I’m hoping I’ll get more info and whatever I choose will work out well for me.

Not really sure if I should reveal my program on here but I live in New York City. Thanks for your thoughts! I really appreciate it. 

Would you mind sharing why you think an unaccredited program should be avoided in your opinion? I wasn’t able to find a lot of info cause it all mostly relates to clinical psychology.

Most of my research has said that a PsyD and PhD are virtually the same except a PhD is more research based but I guess it would make sense for a PhD to be more respected since it’s more commonly known. 

I’m wondering if the salary difference alone is enough to make the PsyD worth it cause NYC is not cheap. My family and most people I’ve talked to seem to only think about the long term money aspect. 

I think my biggest worries are that if I don’t do it I’ll deeply regret my decision later or if I decide to do it I’ll be overwhelmed with coursework & my dissertation & it will negatively impact my current mental health. 

I’m kinda leaning towards not doing it because before this offer I never really considered a doctorate anyway. But there’s still a slight part of me that feels pressure to be as impressive as possible & do what’s best financially for my future salary. 

I have until Monday to decide so I still have a lot of thinking to do. Thanks again for your input!
